question_record.context: During a security incident on host 'vnevado-win10v', a critical process responsible for enforcing security policies was maliciously altered. Various accounts and processes, including the execution of suspicious commands, were involved in the incident.
question_record.question: Can you determine the specific active malware detected following the modification of the critical security process?
solution: The LSASS process memory on the host with AadDeviceId `4d8d23e9-a77d-4e33-9435-b8c457e57ca1` was modified.
Active malware named `mimikatz.exe` was detected running on the same host.

115.name: LSASS process memory modified
115.description: The Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) process enforces security policy by verifying user logons and password changes. Attackers might modify LSASS memory to bypass security mechanisms or circumvent legitimate checks.

150.name: Active unknown malware was detected
150.description:
Malware and unwanted software are undesirable applications that perform annoying, disruptive, or harmful actions on affected machines. Some of these undesirable applications can replicate and spread from one machine to another. Others are able to receive commands from remote attackers and perform activities associated with cyber attacks.

A malware is considered active if it is found running on the machine or it already has persistence mechanisms in place. Active malware detections are assigned higher severity ratings.

Because this malware was active, take precautionary measures and check for residual signs of infection.

interpretation.scope: official graph witness, not a proof of causality, actor identity or autonomous planning
